subject: Margin protection: NeuroPulse commercial exception request
messages:
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeuroPulse: exceptional commercial ask — need VP/CFO path

Team — forwarding NeuroPulse's term sheet (attached) and the ARR impact model. TL;DR: they are pushing for 45% off list for a three-year, multi-region commitment to secure exclusive deployment in a regional cloud partner. Customer rationale: long onboarding, integration investment, and potential co-sell.

Why I'm escalating: at 45% the modeled LTV contribution is below our current threshold for enterprise bespoke discounts; this materially impacts margin in year 1. They have asked for the discount in writing and are expecting an executive decision by Friday.

Asks:
- Marissa: can you outline the commercial levers (ramp credits, usage floors, go-to-market commitments) that could close the gap without giving a straight 45%?
- Kimberly: quick read on precedent and whether we can attach legal/packaging controls (no resale, restricted data residency, SLA carveouts).
- Evelyn: need formal VP/CFO read — if we cannot stay above our minimum margin, will you authorize an exception and under what conditions?

Attachments: NeuroPulse_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf; ARR_impact_model.xlsx

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeuroPulse: exceptional commercial ask — need VP/CFO path

Markus — thanks for the context and the model. A few quick thoughts after a skim:

1) Value levers that reduce the discount need to be explicit: a) 24-month minimum trailing usage floor at 65% of committed, b) one-time onboarding credit capped and amortized, c) co-marketing commitment and two executive references.
2) Precedent: we can stretch to ~35% discount with hard usage guarantees and a true-up. Anything above 35% historically went to CFO review.
3) Packaging idea: remove the premium SLA on year 1 and offer a conditional upgrade in year 2 if usage targets are met — reduces our near-term cost.

If we present this as a structured concession (35% discount + $150k onboarding credit amortized over 3 years + 65% ramp floor + co-sell commitment) we keep margin impact contained and preserve governance.

I'll draft a memo with option A (35%, limited credit) and option B (38% + stronger GTM commitments) for FYI.

– Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NeuroPulse: exceptional commercial ask — need VP/CFO path

Markus / Marissa — quick legal & precedent note:

- Precedent: we have approved discounts above 40% only twice in the last 18 months; both required a signed executive concession memo and CFO signoff.
- Controls to include: explicit non-resale clause, limited sub-licensing rights, and a data residency addendum restricting storage to US regions (their ask covers EU workstreams but we can gate that).
- Financial guardrails: CFO must sign off if net effective discount > 35% or if the onboarding credit amortization exceeds $400k in present value.

I recommend we propose a 38% commercial discount but pair it with: 1) 75% initial usage floor for 12 months, 2) a $125k onboarding credit amortized over 24 months with true-up, 3) strict packaging controls (no resale, restricted region), and 4) an exec-level service review at 9 months.

I'll prepare a redline for the term sheet and flag the clauses Kimberly references.

– Kimberly Park
VP, Commercial Legal | Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing memo: recommended concession package for NeuroPulse (for VP/CFO sign-off)

Evelyn — attaching a short memo (NP_Pricing_Memo_20270407.docx) with the recommended path. Summary below:

Recommended offer (balanced):
- Net discount: 38% off list on base model pricing
- Commitment: 3-year term, annual true-ups, minimum annual consumption 75% of committed capacity in year 1
- Onboarding: $125,000 onboarding credit, amortized over 24 months, subject to usage true-up
- Packaging & controls: no resale, US-region data residency for initial term; premium SLA deferred to year 2 conditional on usage
- Commercial concessions contingent on a signed PR/Co-sell MOU and a revenue milestone at month 9

Rationale: keeps most of the upside for RW while giving NeuroPulse the large headline discount they want to secure partner onboarding. Margin impact (see ARR_impact_model.xlsx) is acceptable at the 38% level with the above controls.

Please reply with explicit VP/CFO decision language. If you want to move this to CFO signoff I can route the exec memo and include the legal redlines.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing memo: recommended concession package for NeuroPulse (for VP/CFO sign-off)

Markus / team — reviewed the memo and the model. I agree we should pursue a controlled concession but we need slightly firmer guardrails before I escalate to CFO. Conditions for my approval to route to CFO:

1) Reduce headline discount to 36% (I understand this is 200bp lower than proposed — present as a range 36–38% dependent on final usage floor).
2) Increase year-1 minimum consumption to 80% of committed capacity or include a backstop true-up of up to 10% of the onboarding credit if minimums aren't met.
3) Remove any open-ended co-marketing commitment; replace with a defined 6-month pilot reference and two joint press mentions maximum.
4) Require a clause that allows us to pause premium features if operational cost exceeds forecasted thresholds for two consecutive months.

If Markus can confirm these edits (I realize this tightens the package materially), I'll approve escalation to CFO for final sign-off. Please prepare a two-page exec memo that states the revised ask, the financial delta versus baseline, and the recommended sign-off language for CFO.

– Evelyn Hart
VP, Finance | Redwood Inference
